partNotes.LedgeJumpEntry:
Ledge jump: the player steps off a ledge and falls until the ground test under the feet passes. Available to every form; only the drop attack (CheckLedgeJumpAttack) is Freedan-only.

Three writers put its address into the player actor's entry word ($0000,Y): SouthLedgeTile (player_move_south) when the player walks south onto a type $08 cell, and the one-shot scene scripts awB3_ledge_jump_trigger (Angkor Wat outer north) and pyD0_breakable_wall (Pyramid scenes $D0 and $D1). The scripts enter it with no $08 cell involved.

Entry: clear actor flag $0008 (restored by LedgeJumpLand), set actor flag $0200, hide the use-item button ($0008) via joypadMaskStd. Plays the take-off poses (sprites #18, #19).

Main loop: 3-sprite alternating cycle (#1A, #1B, #19) with force Y movement (#07 = downward). Each pass checks for solid ground (landing). CheckLedgeJumpFrame reads the $2A event flag for animation timing. CheckLedgeJumpAttack gates the drop attack to Freedan (characterForm == 1) with abilityBitmask bit 6 ($0040).

Mesen2, scene $01: pose $18 for about 24 frames at the edge, then the fall at about 4 px per frame (y 361 to 448), pose $1C for the landing; playerFlags $0808 and actor flags $8700 throughout.
partNotes.LedgeJumpLand: Landing of a ledge jump: plays sound #2C and the landing pose #1C, restores actor flag $0008, clears $0200 and the use-item hide, and returns to PlayerIdleEntry.

partNotes.SouthLedgeTile:
Type $08 cell reached while walking south: the start of a ledge jump. The old names (SouthStairsTile, then SouthVineTile) were wrong: nothing here is a stair, a vine or a ladder. In Mesen2 (scene $01, South Cape) the player walks into the gap of a mossy wall edge, steps off and falls onto the roof below. It is south-only because a ledge can only be jumped down from the north; the north handler treats the cell as a wall.

$08 is a real collision type, not a script flag: 59 of the 223 map scenes hold it (Angkor Wat, the Pyramid, Sky Garden, the Great Wall, Freejia, the Gold Ship, Incan Ruins, South Cape, Edward's Castle, Itory and others; B1 census, plans/extracted-audit/mesen2-results). Only South Cape was watched; the other scenes are assumed to be ledges of the same kind. The Mt. Temple scenes $A0-$A9 hold no $02, $07 or $08 cell.

Entry rule: column-aligned (carry clear): go straight in. Straddling (carry set): the cell to the RIGHT must also be type $08, otherwise blocked. Sets playerFlags $0800 (script / ability lock) through the high byte playerStateByte, switches the player to LedgeJumpEntry (which sets actor flag $0200 and hides the use-item button), clears the wait counter and floors Y through SnapYSouthCollision (which also zeroes playerSpeedNs).

blockNote: Angkor Wat outer north (scene $B3): one-shot trigger that changes the map and then makes the player jump (LedgeJumpEntry).

Spawned once, by scene_B3_actors. The actor dies at once when flag word $016E is set. Otherwise it waits (SetEntryHere) until the player stands in the tile box (6A, 0C)-(6F, 0D), then: ORs $CFFC into joypadMaskStd 20 times (LoopStart #14), plays the sound pair #$0F0F, applies BG change #6E (StageBgChange / ApplyBgChange), sets flag word $016E, writes player_character.LedgeJumpEntry into the player actor (address at +$00, bank byte at +$02, $08 and $2A zeroed), sets playerFlags $0800 and dies.

The jump starts because this script writes LedgeJumpEntry, not because of a type $08 cell. BG change #6E was not decoded or viewed. The earlier names and notes (awB3_vine_reveal, 'grows vines', 'draw the vine tiles', 'ladder trigger') were guesses; what the change draws and where the player lands was not watched.

Pyramid scenes $D0 and $D1 (one placement each): one-shot trigger that draws two metatiles, applies a BG change and then makes the player jump (LedgeJumpEntry). The old note (hit points, debris, 'used extensively in the maze-like corridors') does not match the code: there is no HP counter, no hit test and no spawn, and only two scenes place it. The block name (breakable wall) is probably wrong as well and was not changed because the purpose of the trigger was not established.

The actor's $0E word (copied to $26) picks the variant: 0 uses flag word $0170 and BG change #70, anything else flag word $0171 and BG change #71. The actor dies at once when its flag word is set. Otherwise each pass first requires the player's $7F0008 byte to be $95 or $8E and the player's animation index ($28) to be $1C; what those values mean was not traced ($1C is the landing pose of a ledge jump, LedgeJumpLand, and other player code stages it too). Then BranchIfPlayerNear #01 leads to the action code. The first pass through it (the actor's $24 is 0) sets $24 = 1, converts the actor's $14 / $16 to tile coordinates (saved in orbitAngle / orbitDiameter, restored afterwards) and draws metatiles #E8 and #E9 side by side with DrawMetatileHere. A later pass ($24 nonzero) plays sound #15, applies the BG change, sets the flag word, clears actor flag $0008 and sets $0200 in the player's $10, writes player_character.LedgeJumpEntry into the player actor (address +$00, bank byte +$02, $08 and $2A zeroed) and dies.
As in awB3_ledge_jump_trigger, the jump starts because this script writes LedgeJumpEntry, with no type $08 cell involved.
